data.name: Balbhadra
data.gender_notes: Balbhadra is used as a male name in Hindu naming traditions.
data.long_meaning: Balbhadra is a Sanskrit name derived from two roots: 'Bal' meaning power and 'Bhadra' meaning generous. This name is attributed to Lord Vishnu, who is revered for his immense power and his generous nature towards his devotees. The name Balbhadra carries the meaning “Powerful and generous” and is chosen by families in Hindu traditions for the positive qualities it expresses. Linguistically it belongs to the Sanskrit tradition and is also used in Hindi, Sanskrit, Marathi. Parents who choose Balbhadra usually hope their child will grow to embody powerful and generous and live with faith, good character and purpose.
data.spiritual_meaning: A name that invokes blessings of Lord Vishnu, symbolizing power, generosity, and spiritual growth.
data.etymology: Balbhadra belongs to the Sanskrit linguistic tradition and is used in Hindu naming. Its recorded meaning is “Powerful and generous.”
data.numerology_meaning: In Pythagorean numerology the letters of Balbhadra total 4, giving a life-path number of 4. Number 4 is linked with Rahu and with the qualities of stability, discipline and hard work.

vedic_reference.note: Balbhadra is not a name directly mentioned in the Vedas or Indian mythology. However, the name can be derived from the Sanskrit words बल (bal) meaning 'strength' and भद्र (bhadra) meaning 'auspicious'.

historical_references.reference: Balbhadra, also known as Balavadra, was a king of the Vatsa dynasty, which ruled over the region of Magadha in ancient India, around 365-338 BC. He was a contemporary and ally of Emperor Chandragupta Maurya.
historical_references.context: Ancient India, Magadha region, Vatsa dynasty, contemporary and ally of Emperor Chandragupta Maurya

historical_references.reference: Balbhadra was also a general in the army of the Satavahana king Gautamiputra Satakarni, who ruled over the Deccan plateau in southern India, around 130-158 AD. Balbhadra is best known for his victory over the Shaka invader Rudradaman I at the Battle of Kalinga.
historical_references.context: Ancient India, Deccan plateau, Satavahana dynasty, victory over Shaka invader Rudradaman I at the Battle of Kalinga

Today, this name is popular on social media platforms like Instagram, where users share images and stories related to Balbhadra and Hindu mythology.
